demography.title: Demography of India — Population Dynamics & Demographic Transition

keyMetrics.totalPopulation: 1,210,854,977 (Census 2011: 1.21 billion; surpassed 1.43 billion in 2023, making India the most populous nation)
keyMetrics.populationDensity: 382 persons per sq km (Bihar highest among states at 1,106; Arunachal Pradesh lowest at 17; Delhi highest among UTs at 11,320)
keyMetrics.overallSexRatio: 943 females per 1,000 males (Kerala highest at 1,084; Puducherry 1,037; Haryana lowest among states at 879; Daman & Diu lowest UT at 618)
keyMetrics.childSexRatio06: 919 females per 1,000 males (alarming drop from 927 in 2001; Mizoram highest at 970; Haryana lowest at 834)
keyMetrics.literacyRate: 73.0% (Males: 80.9%, Females: 64.6%; Kerala highest at 94.0%, Bihar lowest at 61.8%)
keyMetrics.totalFertilityRate: 2.0 (NFHS-5, 2019-21: below replacement level of 2.1; only Bihar, Meghalaya, and UP remain slightly above replacement level)

demographicTransition.theory: Warren Thompson & Frank Notestein Demographic Transition Model (DTM) tracing birth and death rate transitions across industrialization.
demographicTransition.stage1: High Stationary: High birth rate and high fluctuating death rate (epidemics, famines); population growth slow. India was in Stage 1 before 1921.
demographicTransition.greatDivide: 1921 — 'The Year of the Great Divide': Only census where India recorded NEGATIVE population growth (-0.31%) due to 1918 Spanish Flu pandemic and famine. Post-1921, mortality declined steadily while fertility stayed high.
demographicTransition.stage2: Early Expanding: High birth rate, steeply declining death rate; rapid population explosion (India during 1951–1981).
demographicTransition.stage3: Late Expanding: Rapidly falling birth rate, low death rate; population growth decelerates (India's current stage post-1991, with TFR reaching 2.0).
demographicTransition.stage4: Low Stationary: Low birth rate and low death rate; stable population (Kerala and Tamil Nadu approaching Stage 4).

demographicDividend.definition: Economic growth potential when the share of working-age population (15–64 years) is higher than the dependent population (<15 and >65 years).
demographicDividend.medianAge: India's median age is ~28.7 years (compared to 38 in China and US, 48 in Japan), providing a demographic window of opportunity until ~2045–2055.
demographicDividend.prerequisites: Requires substantial investments in human capital: healthcare, high-quality skilling (Skill India), vocational training, and formal job creation to avert a 'demographic disaster'.

urbanization.title: Urbanization in India — Trends, Metropolises & Smart Infrastructure
urbanization.censusDefinition: Urban Area in Census of India: (1) Statutory Towns: Municipal corporation, municipality, cantonment board, or notified town area; (2) Census Towns: Population ≥ 5,000; at least 75% of male main working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits; density ≥ 400 persons per sq km.

urbanTrends.urbanPopulation: 377.1 million in 2011 (31.16% of total); projected to cross 600 million (>40%) by 2036.
urbanTrends.highestUrbanState: Goa (62.2% urban), followed by Mizoram (52.1%) and Tamil Nadu (48.4%). Among large states, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra (45.2%), and Gujarat (42.6%) are most urbanized.
urbanTrends.lowestUrbanState: Himachal Pradesh (only 10.0% urban), followed by Bihar (11.3%) and Assam (14.1%).
urbanTrends.megacities: Greater Mumbai (18.4 million), Delhi (16.3 million), Kolkata (14.1 million) — Census 2011.

urbanChallenges.issues: Proliferation of informal settlements / slums (e.g. Dharavi in Mumbai); severe shortage of affordable housing; urban heat islands (UHI); loss of blue-green infrastructure (encroachment of urban wetlands in Chennai, Bengaluru, Delhi causing severe urban deluges); inadequate municipal sewage and solid waste processing; traffic gridlock.
urbanChallenges.schemes: Smart Cities Mission (100 smart cities with integrated command and control centers / ICCC); AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation — universal water tap and sewerage coverage); Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U); Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U 2.0); PM e-Bus Sewa.

census.title: History & Framework of the Indian Census

history.event: First non-synchronous Census of India conducted under British Viceroy Lord Mayo.
First complete, synchronous decennial Census conducted under Viceroy Lord Ripon (Census Commissioner W.C. Plowden). Decennial census conducted uninterrupted every 10 years until 2011.
Census Act 1948 enacted, establishing permanent statutory authority.
Office of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) created under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
15th National Census (7th post-independence), conducted in two phases: House listing & Housing Census, followed by Population Enumeration.
First fully Digital Census of India featuring self-enumeration mobile portals, geo-referenced digital mapping, and seamless demographic analytics.

census.secc: Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC 2011): Conducted by Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation, and MHA to identify beneficiary households based on deprivation indicators for social welfare schemes (Ayushman Bharat, PMAY, Ujjwala).

industrialRegions.drivers: Cotton textile origin, cheap hydel power from Western Ghats (Tata Hydro), Bombay High oil & petrochemicals, financial capital access, engineering, IT (Pune), and automobile hub.
Jute textile belt along Hooghly river, early British capital, proximity to Raniganj coal and Damodar mineral hinterland, cheap labour from Bihar/Odisha, Kolkata port.

Heavy public sector investment (HAL, BHEL, ISRO), Pykara & Mettur hydel power, cotton textiles (Coimbatore Manchester of South India), IT & electronics (Bengaluru), automobile and hardware cluster (Chennai).
Black soil cotton belt, petrochemicals and refineries (Kandla, Jamnagar, Dahej), chemical and pharmaceutical corridors, diamond cutting (Surat), port-led industrial growth.
The Ruhr of India — co-location of Gondwana coal (Jharia, Bokaro), high-grade hematite iron ore (Singhbhum, Kendujhar), manganese, limestone, and water from DVC; heavy engineering and steel plants.
Port-based Visakhapatnam steel plant, Hindustan Shipyard, petroleum refinery, fertilizers, Krishnapatnam port corridor, pharmaceuticals.
National capital consumer market, automobiles (Maruti Suzuki Gurugram-Manesar), IT & electronics (Noida, Gurugram), light engineering, apparel.
Agricultural processing (coir, cashew nut processing), fish canning, titanium dioxide, titanium sponge, IT (Technopark Thiruvananthapuram).

roads.totalLength: ~63.7 lakh km (second largest road network in the world after USA)
roads.nationalHighways: Over 146,000 km (~2% of road length, carrying >40% of total road traffic)
roads.goldenQuadrilateral: 5,846 km 4/6-lane highway connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata
roads.northSouthEastWest: NS: Srinagar to Kanyakumari (NH-44, 4,000 km); EW: Silchar to Porbandar (NH-27, 3,300 km); crossing at Jhansi (UP)
roads.bharatmala: Umbrella highway development program developing 34,800 km of economic corridors, border/coastal connectivity, and greenfield expressways (Delhi-Mumbai, Delhi-Amritsar-Katra, Bengaluru-Chennai)

railways.network: Fourth largest national railway system under single management (~68,000 route km; >90% broad gauge electrified)
railways.dfc: Dedicated Freight Corridors: Western DFC (1,506 km: Dadri, UP to JNPT, Mumbai) and Eastern DFC (1,875 km: Ludhiana to Dankuni, WB) built to separate heavy freight from passenger lines
railways.modernization: Vande Bharat semi-high speed trains; Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (bullet train, 508 km using Japanese Shinkansen E5 technology)

waterwaysAndPorts.inlandWaterways: 111 National Waterways declared under National Waterways Act 2016. Major: NW-1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly: Prayagraj to Haldia, 1,620 km with multi-modal terminals at Varanasi, Sahibganj, Haldia); NW-2 (Brahmaputra: Sadiya to Dhubri, 891 km); NW-3 (West Coast Canal, Kerala: Kottapuram to Kollam, 205 km with 24-hr navigation)
waterwaysAndPorts.majorPorts: 12 Major Ports (6 West Coast: Deendayal/Kandla, Mumbai, JNPT, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin; 6 East Coast: VO Chidambaranar/Tuticorin, Chennai, Kamarajar/Ennore, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Syama Prasad Mookerjee/Kolkata-Haldia). Largest container port: JNPT; Deepest natural harbour: Visakhapatnam; Riverine port: Kolkata; Corporatized major port: Kamarajar/Ennore
waterwaysAndPorts.sagarmala: Port-led development program modernizing ports, port-linked industrialization (Coastal Economic Zones / CEZs), and coastal community development

civilAviation.udan: Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik: Regional connectivity scheme providing capped airfares and Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to revive unserved and underserved airstrips across Tier-2/Tier-3 cities.

pipelines.networks: Cross-country energy pipelines: HVJ Pipeline (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur, 1,750 km first cross-country gas pipeline); Urja Ganga Gas Pipeline (Jagdishpur-Haldia & Bokaro-Dhamra, 2,655 km connecting Eastern India); Salaya-Mathura crude pipeline; Barauni-Kanpur products pipeline.
